Article Title: Savarkar remark: Supreme Court quashes case against Rahul Gandhi
Article Text:
Rahul had allegedly described Savarkar as a “receiver of pension from Britishers” and “a servant of Britishers” at a news conference in 2022.

Noting that there was no sanction to prosecute leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Gandhi for his remarks against V D Savarkar, Supreme Court Friday quashed proceedings against him initiated by a Lucknow court. Rahul had allegedly described Savarkar as a "receiver of pension from Britishers" and "a servant of Britishers" at a news conference in 2022. SC, which had given an earful to Rahul at the last hearing, concluded that criminal proceedings against him were untenable for want of sanction. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu allowed Rahul's appeal on the ground of lack of sanction, even before senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi could argue the case on behalf of the Congress MP.
Article Summary: Supreme Court quashes proceedings against him initiated by a Lucknow court. Rahul had allegedly described Savarkar as a “receiver of pension from Britishers’ and “a servant of Britishers" at a news conference in 2022. SC concluded that criminal proceedings against Rahul were untenable for want of sanction.

Article Title: Privilege notice against Rahul Gandhi over remarks against Amit Shah
Article Text:
Rahul had claimed Shah’s hand in police excesses against student protesters.

Taking cognisance of two BJP MPs’ complaints against Rahul Gandhi for levelling “defamatory” allegations against home minister Amit Shah, Lok Sabha secretariat has sought the leader of the opposition’s reply to Speaker Om Birla by Aug 28. The MPs, Sanjay Jaiswal and Anurag Thakur, had filed separate complaints to Birla, accusing Rahul of violating parliamentary rules during his speech in the House on July 30.Rahul had claimed Shah’s hand in police excesses against student protesters. Official sources said Birla would decide whether to ask the House’s privilege committee to look into the allegations or close the matter after taking note of Rahul’s response.

Lok Sabha secretariat has sought the leader of the opposition’s reply to Speaker Om Birla by Aug 28. The MPs, Sanjay Jaiswal and Anurag Thakur, had filed separate complaints.

Article Title: Be mindful of strong India-Italy ties, says MEA after Rahul's jibe at Modi & Meloni
Article Text:
At an event Thursday, Rahul had ridiculed PM Modi’s handling of foreign policy.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs Friday urged everyone to be mindful of strong India-Italy ties and the need to be respectful to each other. The remark followed a controversy over Congress member of Parliament Rahul Gandhi as well as party neta Sandeep Dikshit's jibe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi on foreign policy that involved Italian PM Giorgia Meloni."We have strong ties with Italy. Our ties with Italy in recent years have expanded and strengthened in every which way, and it's important that, as part of diplomatic practice, we strengthen our ties, keeping in mind being respectful of each other. There's mutual understanding between the two sides," said spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.At an event Thursday, Rahul had ridiculed Modi's handling of foreign policy. The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha said it had somehow been ingrained in Modi's mind that foreign policy was all about hugging leaders. He then hugged Dikshit in a bid to demonstrate what govt's foreign policy was about. "Imagine the ignorance... where did he get the idea...?" he said.Dikshit then said to Rahul, "Ek cheez pooch sakta hoon? Meloni samajh ke toh nahi pakda tha?" Rahul responded, "I have not reached there yet."
Article Summary: The ministry of external affairs Friday urged everyone to be mindful of strong India-Italy ties and the need to be respectful to each other. The remark followed a controversy over Congress member of Parliament Rahul Gandhi as well as party neta Sandeep Dikshit's jibe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Article Title: Lok Sabha panel seeks Rahul Gandhi's response on privilege notices over remarks against Amit Shah
Article Text:
Two BJP MPs have moved motion against Rahul Gandhi.

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has sent notice to the leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi , seeking a response to two separate complaints alleging a breach of privilege over his remarks against Union home minister Amit Shah during a debate on the anti-paper leak bill.The secretariat has asked the Congress leader to submit his reply by August 28, news agency PTI reported.The complaints were filed by BJP MPs Anurag Thakur and Sanjay Jaiswal, who alleged that Rahul Gandhi used "unparliamentary" and "derogatory" language against the Home Minister during the debate on the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.Jaiswal, who is also the BJP's chief whip in the Lok Sabha, shared copies of the communication sent to Rahul Gandhi and his own complaint against the Leader of the Opposition.In his July 29 complaint to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, Jaiswal sought action against Rahul Gandhi under the Rules of Procedure, alleging that the Congress leader's remarks against Amit Shah were unparliamentary.A day later, Anurag Thakur submitted a separate complaint, accusing Rahul Gandhi of using "unparliamentary and derogatory language" and making serious allegations against the home minister without providing adequate advance notice under parliamentary rules.Thakur also alleged a breach of privilege and contempt of the House.In its communication to Rahul Gandhi, the Lok Sabha secretariat said it was forwarding copies of the two complaints and requested him to submit his comments by August 28 for the Speaker's consideration.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday set aside a Lucknow trial court’s order summoning leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi in a criminal defamation case over his remarks about VD Savarkar.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that the required sanction had not been obtained in the matter."Additional Solicitor General and advocate for complainant, in the affidavit filed by UP, submits there is no disclosure of sanction. In such view of the matter, the complaint and orders passed by magistrate stands quashed," the bench said.The defamation case stems from Rahul Gandhi’s remarks about Savarkar during a rally in Maharashtra’s Akola district on November 17, 2022, held as part of his Bharat Jodo Yatra.On April 4, 2025, the Lucknow bench of the high court said Rahul Gandhi could file a revision petition before the sessions court, holding that its intervention was not required at that stage.The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha had challenged the subordinate court’s order summoning him while contesting the ongoing proceedings in the case.Satyaki Savarkar, VD Savarkar’s grandnephew, had filed a complaint against Rahul, alleging that during a speech in London in March 2023, the Congress leader claimed that V D Savarkar had written in a book about an incident in which he and five to six friends beat up a Muslim man and that he felt happy about it.Satyaki Savarkar claimed that no such incident took place and that VD Savarkar had never written about any such episode. He sought Rahul Gandhi’s conviction under Section 500 of the IPC and compensation under Section 357 of the CrPC.The court had already granted bail to Rahul Gandhi in the case.
Article Summary: The defamation case stems from Rahul Gandhi’s remarks about Savarkar during a rally in Maharashtra. The court had already granted bail to Rahul Gandhi in the case. The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha challenged the subordinate court's order summoning him while contesting the ongoing proceedings.

Article Title: Dindoshi Court Grants Anticipatory Bail to API Devendra Kate in Sexual Assault Case
Article Text:
Mumbai





: The Dindoshi Sessions Court granted anticipatory bail to Assistant Police Inspector (API) Devendra Kate in a case registered by Amboli Police alleging sexual relations on a false promise of marriage, forced termination of pregnancy and criminal intimidation.Additional Sessions Judge Neeta S. Anekar allowed Kate’s anticipatory bail registered under BNS sections 69, 89 and 351(2) of rape, causing a miscarriage without the woman’s consent and criminal intimidation. The court granted anticipatory bail to Kate on a personal bond of ₹50,000 with one or two sureties.According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that she came into contact with Kate in 2024 while pursuing a criminal complaint. Their friendship allegedly developed into a romantic relationship. The woman claimed that Kate established physical relations with her on the promise of marriage at hotels in Amboli and continued the relationship over several months. She further alleged that he induced her to terminate two pregnancies and later avoided her, leading her to attempt suicide.Seeking pre-arrest bail, Kate, through his lawyer Karan Mehta, denied the allegations and contended that the relationship was consensual.He argued that the complainant was fully aware of his marital status and had voluntarily continued the relationship. The defence also submitted that the allegations were made after he refused further monetary demands.The prosecution and the complainant opposed the application expressed apprehension that the applicant, being a police officer, could influence witnesses.After examining the FIR and case diary, the court observed that the complainant was an educated and socially active woman who had been in a relationship with the applicant for a considerable period. The court noted that the relationship continued even after the first alleged termination of pregnancy, indicating a prima facie consensual relationship between two adults.The judge held that whether the promise of marriage was false from the inception and whether the complainant was unaware of the applicant’s marital status were issues that would have to be decided during trial. The court further observed that the grounds cited for custodial interrogation were not justified at this stage.The court directed him to cooperate with the investigation, refrain from influencing witnesses, not tamper with evidence, not leave India without permission and not contact the complainant during the investigation, inquiry or trial. Any breach of the conditions would result in cancellation of bail.
Article Summary: Dindoshi Sessions Court granted anticipatory bail to Assistant Police Inspector (API) Devendra Kate in a case registered by Amboli Police. The case alleges sexual relations on a false promise of marriage, forced termination of pregnancy and criminal intimidation. Kate denied the allegations and contended that the relationship was consensual.

Article Title: Bombay high court refuses to quash criminal proceedings against Akbaruddin Owaisi
Article Text:
Justice Joshi observed that an elected representative was expected to understand the consequences of such comments and that the speech appeared “planned”, “measured” and “predetermined”.

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high court has refused to quash criminal proceedings against AIMIM MLA Akbaruddin Owaisi over a speech delivered at a 2011 election rally in Nanded saying that freedom of speech is not an unfettered right and cannot be used to deliberately hurt religious sentiments.In an order passed on Aug 6, Justice R M Joshi dismissed Owaisi’s plea challenging the FIR, chargesheet and a magistrate’s 2021 order issuing process under sections 295A and 298 of the Indian Penal Code. The case stems from a complaint filed by BJP MLA Rajasingh T Naval Singh Lodh, who alleged that Owaisi made derogatory remarks against Lord Ram and members of his community.Rejecting Owaisi’s contention that the case was barred by limitation, the court relied on the Supreme Court’s 2025 ruling in Ghanshyam Soni vs State (Govt of NCT of Delhi) and held that limitation is computed from the date of filing of the complaint or initiation of proceedings, not from the date cognisance is taken.The court noted that Owaisi’s speech was delivered on Dec 8, 2011, while the complaint was filed within the prescribed period. It further held that the charge under section 298 could proceed along with the more serious offence under section 295A.Examining the substance of the speech, Justice Joshi observed that Owaisi initially referred to the Allahabad high court’s Ram Janmabhoomi judgment but later made remarks which, prima facie, appeared intended to mock Lord Ram and wound the sentiments of his followers.The court declined to reproduce the alleged remarks to avoid further publicity but said the statements appeared to be neither casual nor spontaneous.Justice Joshi observed that an elected representative was expected to understand the consequences of such comments and that the speech appeared “planned”, “measured” and “predetermined”.Referring to the ingredients of section 295A, the court said deliberate and malicious intent must be assessed in the context of the words used as well as their tone, pitch and manner of delivery.“Tolerance cannot be misconstrued/misunderstood to there being a licence to intentionally hurt the religious feelings of others,” Justice Joshi observed.The court further said constitutional values such as liberty, tolerance and fraternity do not provide protection for deliberate acts intended to outrage religious sentiments. It distinguished judgments cited by the defence, noting that those cases lacked allegations or evidence of deliberate and malicious intent. In contrast, the material placed on record in the present case prima facie indicated apparently outrageous statements and a triable case, it noted.The court also took note of the prosecution’s submission that the speech continues to be available online, calling it a serious concern as it could perpetuate the alleged insult. While refraining from issuing directions in the absence of necessary parties, the court expressed hope that govt would take appropriate action.Dismissing the petition, the high court clarified that its observations were only prima facie and should not influence the trial court while deciding the case on merits.
Article Summary: The Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high court has refused to quash criminal proceedings against AIMIM MLA Akbaruddin Owaisi. The case stems from a complaint filed by BJP MLA Rajasingh T Naval Singh Lodh, who alleged that O Waisi made derogatory remarks against Lord Ram and members of his community.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi to visit Pune on Aug 22
Article Text:
Pune:





Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi will visit Pune on Aug 22 to participate in ‘Chhatron ki Goonj’ initiative by the Congress.Announcing Rahul’s visit to Pune, state Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal on Friday said Gandhi will interact with students during his visit. “Before Pune, Rahul participated in ‘Chhatron ki Goonj’ initiative in Kota, Dehradun and Prayagraj cities where he spoke to the students to understand their issues. In a similar manner, he will interact with girl students in Pune to understand the challenges being faced by them in regards with the education system,” Sapkal said.Rahul’s interaction with the younger generation in Pune will take place against the backdrop of the recent Cockroach Janata Party’s protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi where he and other opposition members raised the issue of violence against the protesters. During his visit to Pune, the Congress leader is expected to target the centre on the recent NEET paper leak issue.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi will visit Pune on Aug 22 to participate in ‘Chhatron ki Goonj’ initiative by the Congress. During his visit to Pune, the Congress leader is expected to target the centre on the recent NEET paper leak issue.

Article Title: Carpenter robbed of ₹30,000 at knifepoint in Ganeshpeth
Article Text: Nagpur: A 32-year-old carpenter from Jharkhand was robbed of ₹30,000 at knifepoint by three unidentified men near Empress Mall Gate in Ganeshpeth on Wednesday afternoon.Complainant Bablu Gopi Mistri Sharma, a resident of Mehernagar, Wathoda, was travelling in an e-rickshaw towards the railway station to return to his native village in Dhanbad when the accused intercepted him around 3.10 pm on Aug 13.Two of them attacked Sharma and threatened to kill him with a knife while the third forcibly snatched the cash from his pocket. The trio then fled on a two-wheeler. Sharma, who works as a carpenter, lodged a complaint the same evening.Police have registered a case under relevant sections of BNS. The accused remain absconding.
Article Summary: A 32-year-old carpenter from Jharkhand was robbed of ₹30,000 at knifepoint by three unidentified men. Bablu Gopi Mistri Sharma was travelling in an e-rickshaw towards the railway station to return to his native village in Dhanbad.

Article Title: Man ends life near railway station
Article Text:
Nagpur:





An unidentified man, aged around 40-45, allegedly ended life by hanging himself near the railway station. His body was found hanging from a tree on the road connecting the Metro station and the Platform 8 gate on Thursday.According to Govt Railway Police (GRP) sources, the man reportedly entered the railway station premises and climbed a tall tree in an isolated section adjoining a nullah.Officials said the man allegedly used the shirt he was wearing to hang himself. The fire brigade and forensic teams reached the spot and carried out the necessary procedures. The body was subsequently sent to Mayo Hospital for postmortem.Police said no injuries were found on the body. The deceased remains unidentified, and efforts are underway to establish his identity and contact his relatives.
Article Summary: Unidentified man, aged around 40-45, allegedly ended life by hanging himself near the railway station. His body was found hanging from a tree on the road connecting the Metro station and the Platform 8 gate on Thursday. Police said no injuries were found on the body.

Article Title: Man gets 20 years in jail for raping minor
Article Text: Chandrapur: District judge-1 and additional sessions judge, Chandrapur PM Gupta on Thursday sentenced Vilas Damodar Randhaye, a resident of Ghodazari in Nagbhid taluka, to 20 years’ rigorous imprisonment for repeatedly sexually assaulting a minor girl and threatening to kill her if she disclosed the abuse.According to the prosecution, Randhaye sexually assaulted the girl several times between May 10 and May 25, 2024, when she was alone at home. The girl subsequently became pregnant. The accused allegedly threatened her with dire consequences if she revealed the abuse.Nagbhid police registered a case under relevant provisions of the IPC and the POCSO Act. Assistant police inspector Anuradha Phukat investigated the case and filed the chargesheet before the court.On Thursday, the court convicted Randhaye under Section 6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced him to 20 years’ rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs2,000, in default, one month of simple imprisonment. He was also sentenced to six months’ rigorous imprisonment under Section 506 of the IPC. Public Prosecutor Sandeep B Nagpure represented the prosecution.
Article Summary: Vilas Damodar Randhaye, a resident of Ghodazari in Nagbhid taluka, was sentenced to 20 years’ rigorous imprisonment for repeatedly sexually assaulting a minor girl. The girl subsequently became pregnant. The accused allegedly threatened her with dire consequences if she revealed the abuse.

Article Title: Utkrisht Seva Medal for Nashik top cop Sandeep Karnik
Article Text:
Sandeep Karnik

Police commissioner Sandeep Karnik has been selected for the Utkrishta Seva Medal among several officers and personnel from Nashik, ahead of Independence Day The Utkrisht Seva Medal and Atiutkrisht Seva Medal are annual state-level honours instituted by the state govt to recognise outstanding, meritorious and dedicated service in the Maharashtra Police.Meanwhile, the President’s Medal for distinguished service has also been announced. Article Title: Is carrying the national flag a sinful act? asks Madras HC
Article Text:
Chennai:





“Is carrying the national flag in a procession a sinful act?” wondered Justice V Lakshminarayanan of the Madras high court . He also questioned whether Coimbatore, where permission for a procession was denied by the local administration, was part of Pakistan or Afghanistan, as restrictions were imposed against carrying the national flag during a procession.The court made the observations while hearing a plea moved by J Rameshkumar, a BJP functionary, challenging the denial of permission for an Independence Day rally on Aug 15.On Friday, when the plea came up for hearing, the Coimbatore police submitted that permission had been denied because the petitioner had sought to conduct the procession on a major road.The proposed route was a crowded area with schools, colleges and a bus stop, and permission could not be granted due to possibility of law-and-order issues, the police said. Permission was however granted for processions at 12 designated spots in Coimbatore, and it was clarified that the govt was not preventing anyone from carrying the national flag.Recording the submissions, the court said, “Freedom fighter Tiruppur Kumaran died holding the national flag during the freedom struggle. In such a country, why should there be a restriction on carrying the national flag?”The court then pointed out that permission had earlier been denied for a procession by the Thanthai Periyar Dravidar Kazhagam (TPDK) and now for the BJP and questioned whether permission was being granted only to the ruling TVK.The court then directed the police to grant permission for the rally on Aug 18 from ARC junction in Mettupalayam Road to Chinthamani from 4pm to 7pm.
Article Summary: The court made the observations while hearing a plea moved by J Rameshkumar, a BJP functionary, challenging the denial of permission for an Independence Day rally. The court then directed the police to grant permission for the rally on Aug 18 from 4pm to 7pm.

Article Title: 12 workers injured as church construction collapses in Thoothukudi
Article Text:
As many as 12 workers suffered minor injuries as the concrete portion of a church which was under collapsed in Thoothukudi on Thursday

Madurai:





Twelve workers suffered minor injuries after a portion of a church under construction collapsed at Vellapatti near Thalamuthu Nagar in Thoothukudi district on Thursday.Construction work was under way at Our Lady of Good Counsel Church when the iron rods supporting a newly laid concrete roof portion slipped, causing part of the structure to collapse. The workers were trapped under the debris.Fire and rescue services personnel rushed to the spot and rescued all 12 workers. They were taken to the government medical college hospital in Thoothukudi for treatment.Thalamuthu Nagar police registered a case and further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: Construction work was under way at Our Lady of Good Counsel Church when the iron rods supporting a newly laid concrete roof portion slipped. Fire and rescue services personnel rushed to the spot and rescued all 12 workers. They were taken to the government medical college hospital in Thoothukudi for treatment.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: 3 cops suspended for taking away money from scrap dealer
Article Text:
AI-image

Kochi

:





Three policemen, including two sub-inspectors, were placed under suspension for allegedly taking over Rs 1 lakh from a scrap dealer during an investigation. Police sources said the suspended officers have been identified as sub-inspectors Sebastian Chacko and Shameer and CPO Jijo.The case pertains to an Assam native, who was arrested by Kalamassery police, escaping and later getting arrested. He had escaped when taken to Aluva district hospital for medical examination in July. The man was arrested for allegedly stealing 60-metre-long copper wires worth Rs 1.5 lakh from Thrikkakara North. The accused was in handcuffs when he escaped. However, when he was later tracked down, he was not wearing the cuffs.Police sources said that the probe team allegedly identified the scrap dealership as having connections to the accused. The allegation was that the officers went to the dealership after arresting him and took over Rs 1 lakh from the cash box of the man who runs the dealership.
Article Summary: Police sources said the suspended officers have been identified as sub- inspectors Sebastian Chacko and Shameer and CPO Jijo. The case pertains to an Assam native, who was arrested by Kalamassery police, escaping and later getting arrested.

Article Title: Mullaperiyar issue: Janasamrakshana Samithi burns effigy of TN chief minister
Article Text:
Janasamrakshana Samithi burns effigy of TN CM Joseph Vijay in Thodupuzha on Friday

Thodupuzha

:





Protesting Tamil Nadu govt’s announcement that the water level in Mullaperiyar Dam would be raised to 152 feet despite Kerala’s opposition, Janasamrakshana Samithi burned an effigy of TN CM Joseph Vijay on Friday.The protest was organised in Thodupuzha as part of the inauguration of the samithi‘s statewide agitation demanding the cancellation of the alleged illegal 999-year lease agreement and decommissioning of Mullaperiyar Dam. Protesters also burned a copy of the lease agreement.The samithi alleged that provisions in the lease agreement renewed in 1970, without discussion in Kerala Legislative Assembly or consultation with experts, had weakened Kerala’s position in the legal battle before Supreme Court.The samithi said Kerala would gain an advantage in the case if the lease agreement was presented before the assembly and a decision taken to cancel it. It also demanded that the state govt convene a special session of the assembly for thepurpose.Samithi office-bearers said Tamil Nadu’s announcement without consulting Kerala and allegedly disregarding the SC verdict was a challenge to the state. They demanded urgent steps from Kerala govt to avert the possibility of a disaster at Mullaperiyar.Samithi general convener P T Sreekumar presided over the protest. Samithi chairperson Roy Varikatt inaugurated the programme. C A Joy, Nixon Kandirikkan, Deepu Karimpani, Jessy Johny, Saju Tharanilam, C N Mani, Sreeraj Chittakkat, Tojo Joseph, Kallarakkal Geethu E G, Babu Mundakkal,Thomas Katangottil, Baby Chembarathi and Shaina Beevi spoke.
Article Summary: Janasamrakshana Samithi burned an effigy of TN CM Joseph Vijay on Friday. The protest was organised in Thodupuzha as part of the inauguration of the samithi’s statewide agitation. Protesters also burned a copy of the lease agreement.
